68: As one might have thought - that is to say, this verse is necessary for the following reason: I might have thought to say: Just as in a case where a lottery is not used to sanctify [an offering], such as with "nests", about which is written "one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering" (Leviticus 5:7) -- if he cast a lot upon them, they are not thereby designated, and he is able to change [their designation], as we have established in Tractate Yoma: "Nests become designated only upon either the owner’s taking of them, when he initially purchases [ and consecrates them for his offering], or upon the priest’s actual performance [of the sacrificial rite upon them]." (Yoma 41a:2)

A verbal designation does effect the consecration - if he said, at the time of taking them, "this one for a sin-offering and this one for a burnt-offering", they are considered designated, and if he alters [the designation], they are disqualified.
Here, in a case in which the use of a lottery does effect the consecration - as is written, "and Aaron will place, etc." (Leviticus 16:8), is it not logically right, etc.
